key_agent_trends: EU institutions advance sovereign AI through equity funding proposals, frontier model compute demos on public supercomputers, and startup awards in strategic sectors.
Agentic systems face dual-use scrutiny after official confirmation of AI-agent cyberattacks on critical infrastructure and first regulated agentic payments.
Open-source coding agents and local models continue to proliferate with modular designs and efficiency optimizations for agent loops.
European Parliament pushes for stronger EU role in global AI governance by supporting city bids to host new UN assessment structures.

stories.headline: European Parliament adopts resolution supporting EU cities' bids to host UN AI governance body
stories.what_happened: On 26 November 2026 the European Parliament adopted a resolution supporting candidacies by EU cities to host a new United Nations pillar for the independent assessment and ethical governance of artificial intelligence. The non-binding resolution backs EU involvement in global AI governance processes under the UN Global Digital Compact and related scientific panel and dialogue mechanisms, without selecting a specific host city or creating the body itself. Italian efforts to promote Milan as a potential host were referenced during debates.
stories.why_it_matters: Signals parliamentary support for positioning Europe as a hub for international AI assessment and ethical governance, complementing the EU AI Act with multilateral influence.

stories.headline: European Commission awards first Apply AI Startup Awards to Better Medicine, Prewave and blueOASIS
stories.what_happened: At the Apply AI Summit on 17 November 2026, Executive Vice-President Henna Virkkunen presented the first Apply AI Startup Awards to three European companies. Better Medicine (Estonia) was recognized for AI-based kidney cancer detection and multi-organ screening. Prewave (Austria) won for AI-powered supply chain intelligence. blueOASIS (Portugal) was awarded for deep-tech ocean monitoring solutions. Selection involved national nominations, expert evaluation and pitching.
stories.why_it_matters: Highlights European AI startups delivering practical applications in healthcare, supply chains and environmental monitoring under the Apply AI Strategy, supporting tech sovereignty through targeted recognition.

stories.headline: Domyn demonstrates ~952B-parameter EUROPA training configuration on JUPITER supercomputer
stories.what_happened: On 12 November 2026 Domyn, lead of the EUROPA consortium with Fraunhofer IAIS and IIS, announced it had run a ~951.9-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts training setup for the Commission-backed open frontier model on Germany's JUPITER exascale supercomputer. The team achieved a 14-fold throughput increase to ~1,300 tokens per second per GPU using 384 NVIDIA GH200 GPUs per replica, estimating a full pre-training run in about four months. Configuration details and engineering fixes were published.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows that Europe can train large-scale open frontier models on existing public EuroHPC infrastructure, advancing sovereign AI capacity without requiring entirely new dedicated clusters.

stories.headline: Switzerland's NCSC confirms first AI-agent cyberattacks on critical infrastructure
stories.what_happened: On 24 November 2026 Switzerland's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC/BACS) confirmed the first reports of cyberattacks against Swiss organisations carried out with the assistance of AI agents, affecting critical infrastructure operators across at least two sectors. Director Florian Schütz later stated there were five confirmed cases, with systems compromised in four of them, including three critical-infrastructure operators. The agency noted that publicly accessible agentic offensive frameworks have nearly doubled since October 2026.
stories.why_it_matters: Provides the first official government count of successful AI-agent breaches on critical infrastructure, underscoring the dual-use risks of agentic frameworks and the need for faster patching and monitoring.

stories.headline: TrueLayer and Papa John's complete first UK agentic Pay by Bank payment
stories.what_happened: On 27 November 2026 TrueLayer announced that a Papa John's AI agent completed the first agentic Pay by Bank payment to a named UK retailer. The pilot, run in the FCA's Supercharged Sandbox with banks including Lloyds and NatWest, used variable recurring payment APIs so the agent paid directly from a linked bank account under customer-set spending limits enforced by the bank. No banking credentials were shared with the agent.
stories.why_it_matters: Demonstrates a practical model for agentic commerce with bank-level spending controls, potentially reducing reliance on card rails while keeping humans in control of mandates.

stories.headline: Pydantic ships Pax, a plugin-first terminal coding agent
stories.what_happened: On 25 November 2026 Pydantic released Pax (pydantic-ai-pax), a beta terminal coding agent built on the Pydantic AI Harness. Every component, including the coding agent itself, is a plugin that can be disabled or replaced, and users can point Pax at their own Pydantic AI agent. It is free and MIT-licensed; vendor benchmarks claim competitive scores on coding tasks at lower token cost than some alternatives.
stories.why_it_matters: Advances modular, composable coding-agent design, making it easier to swap models, sandboxes, and tools without locking into a single harness.

stories.headline: JetBrains releases Mellum2.1 Instruct for faster local agent loops
stories.what_happened: On 25 November 2026 JetBrains released Mellum2.1 Instruct, an Apache 2.0-licensed 12B mixture-of-experts model with 2.5B active parameters that skips chain-of-thought. It is the non-reasoning sibling of Mellum2.1 Thinking and is designed for sub-agents, tool loops, and local execution, using roughly half the tokens of the Thinking variant on agentic coding tasks. JetBrains reports doubled SWE-bench Verified score versus the prior Instruct model.
stories.why_it_matters: Provides a fast, open local model optimised for the high-volume tool calls typical of coding agents, lowering latency and cost for on-device or private deployments.

stories.headline: Cosmic Dawn plans AI-agent OS kernel by end-2026 after $300M seed valuation
stories.what_happened: Bloomberg reported on 27 November 2026 that Chinese AI startup Cosmic Dawn, founded by Baiont Quant founder Feng Ji, raised seed funding at a post-money valuation of about CNY 2 billion (~US$300 million). The company plans to release the kernel of an operating system designed for AI agents by the end of 2026, providing tailored controls for file access, memory, permissions, and multi-agent coordination. Initial deployment is planned inside Baiont Quant.
stories.why_it_matters: Signals growing interest in specialised infrastructure that treats agents as first-class citizens rather than processes running on human-oriented operating systems.
